title: Ema raises $77M as AI starts eating into enterprise software and services
slides: Can Ema's AI replace your enterprise software?
It raised $77M to automate complex workflows.
But it cuts into services revenue, not just software.
Your job may shift from operator to AI supervisor.
Test one repetitive task with Ema today.
thread_text:
1. Your enterprise stack is obsolete

Ema just raised $77M to automate complex workflows that used to require human operators. That's not a feature update — it's a replacement strategy.

2. The hidden revenue threat

Most AI tools sell you software. Ema cuts into the services revenue you bill clients for. That's a bigger disruption than a new competitor.

3. From operator to supervisor

Your daily grind of clicking through repetitive tasks is disappearing. The new job is watching the AI, catching its mistakes, and retraining it. Different skill set, same paycheck — for now.

4. The $77M bet on your workflow

Investors aren't funding a chatbot. They're betting that your most complex, human-heavy processes can run without you. The question is whether you'll be the one supervising it or the one replaced by it.

5. Test one task this week

Pick a repetitive process you do daily. Run it through Ema's free trial or a similar tool. If it saves time, you've just found your new assistant. If it fails, you've found job security. Either way, you learn something real.
